projects.name: CarpetGUI
projects.description: An easy to use GUI for CarpetMod
projects.longDescription:
# English

## Overview

This mod adds three powerful GUI-based visualization features to Carpet Mod, significantly improving the efficiency and user experience of configuring rules and designing systems with Carpet.

---

## Menu

Press **F9** (or your configured menu key)~~(v1.1.0 -) to open a mode selection menu, similar to **F3 + F4**.
![Replace this with a description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/1316e6d2190099d9aa1af53fe3bd3289b7c95fe5_0.webp)~~
---

## Rule Screen

![Replace this with a description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/581859febd5b719105f13d20ae6cfd7194170507.png)

The Rule Screen provides a centralized view of all Carpet rules and vanilla Gamerules, offering a clear and comprehensive interface for browsing and managing them:

* **Full Rule Preview**: Displays all available states and values for each rule
* **State Comparison**: Highlights whether a rule has been modified in real time
* **Favorites**: Mark frequently used rules for quick access
* **Client-side Cache**:
  Allows browsing rules in multiplayer even if the server does not have CarpetGUI installed
* **Save Configuration**: Press **Ctrl + S** to save the current rules as a rule group

> In multiplayer, the interface cannot be opened if the server does not have Carpet installed.
> For the full experience, it is recommended to install CarpetGUI on the server as well.

---

## Rule Group Screen

![Replace this with a description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/f15fe1002c7e46a373eb80af8ebba1fa98d1d842.png)

The Rule Group Screen displays user-defined rule groups and provides a fast and convenient way to switch configurations:

* **Batch Rule Execution**:
  Select a saved rule group and click the button at the bottom-left to execute all included commands at once
* **Create Rule Group**:
  Clicking **New** opens the Rule Screen described above. Changes made here are not applied immediately, but saved as a rule group. A save prompt will appear when exiting
* **Client-side Support**:
  Can be used in multiplayer even if the server does not have CarpetGUI installed

> For the full experience, it is recommended to install CarpetGUI on the server as well.

---

## Rule History Screen

![Replace this with a description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/30f296ccc517bdc56c8a1315a3c2fd1d713320c8.png)

The Rule History Screen provides a lightweight, GitHub-like rule change tracking system, allowing switching, saving, and reverting configurations:

* **Track Rule Changes**:
  Uses a stack-based model.

  * **Push**: Saves the current rule state as a new layer
  * **Revert**: Restores the previous state by removing the top layer
* **Manage Presets**:
  Save rule configurations as presets for different environments and switch between them quickly
* **/rulestack Command**:
  A helper command for servers that integrates with the Rule History Screen.
  Usage mirrors the GUI. `/rulestack prefab` is used for managing presets

> In multiplayer, the interface cannot be opened if the server does not have CarpetGUI installed.

---

# 中文

## 总览

本模组为 Carpet Mod 提供了三个强大的 GUI 可视化功能，旨在显著提升玩家在进行规则配置与工程设计时的效率与使用体验。

---

## 菜单

按下 **F9**（或自定义菜单按键）~~(1.1.0 - )，将弹出一个类似 **F3 + F4** 的模式选择菜单。~~

![Replace this with a description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/2da2e89d3d432a87eceb96f9f49e047cb26555e0.png)

---

## 规则界面

![Replace this with a description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/581859febd5b719105f13d20ae6cfd7194170507.png)

规则界面集中展示所有 Carpet 规则以及原版 Gamerule，提供直观、完整的浏览与管理能力：

* **完整规则预览**：清晰展示每条规则的所有可用状态与取值
* **状态对比**：实时标识规则是否被修改，便于快速定位变更
* **收藏功能**：支持标记常用规则，提高访问效率
* **客户端缓存**：
  即使服务器未安装 CarpetGUI，也可以在多人游戏中浏览规则
* **保存配置**：按下 **Ctrl + S** 可将当前规则保存为规则组

> 在多人游戏中，如果服务器未安装 Carpet，则该界面无法打开。
> 为获得完整功能体验，建议在服务器端同时安装 CarpetGUI。

---

## 规则组界面

![Replace this with a description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/f15fe1002c7e46a373eb80af8ebba1fa98d1d842.png)

规则组界面展示玩家自定义的规则组，提供快速切换和批量配置能力：

* **批量执行规则**：
  选择一个规则组，点击左下角按钮即可一键执行其中所有指令，实现批量修改 Carpet 规则
* **创建规则组**：
  点击“新建”按钮将打开规则界面。此时对规则的修改不会立即应用，而是作为规则组保存；退出界面时会弹出保存提示
* **客户端支持**：
  即使服务器未安装 CarpetGUI，也可以在多人游戏中使用

> 为获得完整功能体验，建议在服务器端同时安装 CarpetGUI。

---

## 规则记录界面

![Replace this with a description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/30f296ccc517bdc56c8a1315a3c2fd1d713320c8.png)

规则记录界面提供类似 GitHub 的轻量级规则变更管理系统，用于规则的切换、存档与回退：

* **规则变更存档**：
  采用栈（Stack）结构管理规则状态：

  * **Push**：保存当前规则状态（入栈）
  * **Revert**：回退至上一个状态（出栈）
* **规则预设管理**：
  可将不同环境所需规则保存为预设，实现快速切换
* **/rulestack 指令**：
  与规则记录界面配合使用的服务器指令，功能与 GUI 基本一致

  * `/rulestack prefab`：用于管理规则预设

> 在多人游戏中，如果服务器未安装 CarpetGUI，则该界面无法打开。

projects.description: Freely blend colors of your pet's collar
projects.longDescription:
### Description 
This is a simple mod that allows your pet's(cats and dogs) collar to be freely dyed and have colors mixed without being limited by the dye types in Minecraft.
### What this mod does
1.Now, when you use dye on your pets, _**the collar color will be a blend of the original color and the dye color**_ , **instead of Mojang's low-quality system that simply overrides the color.**

2.Based on the 24w35a update: **The collar color now defaults to a valid mixed color of the parents' collar colors, unless the mix does not exist or the parents' collar colors cannot be combined.** However, this blending is not ideal. This mod ensures that _**the collar color is truly a blend of the parents' collar colors**_, unaffected by conditions like "the mix does not exist" or "the parents' collar colors cannot be combined.

projects.longDescription:
# This mod has already been merged with [Lucidity](https://modrinth.com/mod/lucidity-mod).

This mod is a powerful tool. It can simulate and display various details of explosions in real-time, including explosion rays, blocks that will be destroyed, the explosion center, estimated damage to nearby entities, and sample points of entities about to be affected.
#IMPORTANT
**_Please check the Changelog for the latest updates!_**

# BASIC COMMANDS
**_/explosionVisualizer mainRender <toggle>_**    <- #Enable Rendering

  
**_/explosionVisualizer renderBlockDestruction <toggle>_** <- #Enable block destruction projection rendering
![Block destruction projection](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/9f31aab6872821ef721d5fcaacee69fb539ae56a.png)
      
**_/explosionVisualizer rendererEntityDamage <toggle>_**   <- #Enable entity damage projection rendering
![Replace this with a description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/7d996031f89320a75841b5085e022f6072026130.png)

**_/explosionVisualizer rendererEntityRaycast <toggle>_**   <- #Enable entity sample-points & raycast rendering
![Replace this with a description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/848899932db90e350755a2f04ebc04fa61468cf3.png)

**/explosionVisualizer renderExplosionBlockDetectionRay <toggle>** <- #Enable explosion sample-points & raycast rendering
![Replace this with a description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/af26ade3f57cafa204b0bc6cac4754ff0d821097.png)

# ADDITIONAL COMMANDS
**/explosionVisualizer fakeExplosion add <name> <x> <y> <z> <power> <IgnorBlockInSide(Boolean)>** <-#create fake explosions
![Replace this with a description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/0806885e5e773f48a58c338f0cc568479c92183c.png)

  **/explosionVisualizer fakeExplosion add <name> <x> <y> <z> <power> <IgnorBlockInside(Boolean)>**
-   <name> : <String>(a name)
-   <x> <y> <z> : <Float> <Float> <Float> (Explosion center's position)
-   <power> : <Float> (Explosion power)
-   <ignoreBlockInside> : <Boolean> (Sometimes the explosion center is inside a block, which affects the evaluation of the explosion. Enabling this option will ignore the block at the explosion center)

**/explosionVisualizer fakeExplosions remove <name>** <-#remove the fake explosion by name

**/explosionVisualizer fakeExplosions removeall**            <-#remove all the fake explosions
![Replace this with a description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/6efeb573c17530a2f641a5358e57d8b64ccfe05b.png)

**/explosionVisualizer blockDamageRayRendererSettings range <Xmax> <Xmin> <Ymax> <Ymin> <Zmax> <Zmin>**

**/explosionVisualizer blockDamageRayRendererSettings range <Xmax> <Xmin> <Ymax> <Ymin> <Zmax> <Zmin>**
- <Xmax> : <Int(0~16)>
- <Xmin> : <Int(0~16)>
- <Ymax> : <Int(0~16)>
- <Ymin> : <Int(0~16)>
- <Zmax> : <Int(0~16)>

- <Xmax> : <Int(0~16)>
- <Xmin> : <Int(0~16)>
- <Ymax> : <Int(0~16)>
- <Ymin> : <Int(0~16)>
- <Zmax> : <Int(0~16)>
- <Zmin> : <Int(0~16)>
are filters to limit the range.

projects.longDescription:
# Litefastica (LitematicaFastMove)

Make Litematica fly.

Features:

- **Independent meshes**: Each placement gets its own GPU meshes (blocks, fluids, overlays). Moving a placement only changes its draw position instead of rebuilding the mesh.
- **Smooth movement**: The displayed position interpolates toward the actual position, so dragging a placement no longer makes it jump one block at a time.
- **Deferred commits**: When a large placement is moved continuously, the placement world is not rewritten at every step. It is committed only after you stop moving.
- **Background building**: Meshes are built in batches of sections across multiple threads, with sections closer to the camera built first. GPU uploads are subject to a per-frame budget to prevent frame stalls.
- **Precise rebuilding**: Only sections near blocks that actually changed in the real world are rebuilt. If the real world is air both before and after a section moves, it is skipped entirely.
- **Multithreaded verification**: The Schematic Verifier in `Configure Schematic Placement` uses multithreaded scanning while continuing to display its results in Litematica's own verification UI.
- **Shader support**: Placements can now theoretically be rendered correctly with any shader pack.

Requires Litematica, malilib, and the bundled [EXIT](https://github.com/hotpad100c/emergency-exit), which allows placement rendering to bypass shader packs.

Supported versions: 26.3 (main branch), 1.21.11, 1.21.8, 1.21.4, 1.21.1, 1.20.6, 1.20.4, 1.20.2, 1.20.1, 1.19.3, 1.18.2, 1.17.1, 1.16.5 (respective `port/<mc>` branches).

## Configuration

All options are injected into Litematica's configuration screen under the Generic tab, in the `--- Litematica Fast Move ---` section.

### Basic

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fastMoveEnabled` Enable | On | Master switch. When disabled, behavior fully reverts to Litematica's original behavior. |
| `fastMoveTakeoverAllPlacements` Take over all placements | On | When enabled, all placements use independent meshes for rendering. When disabled, only placements whose volume is at least `Large Placement Volume` are taken over; smaller ones continue to be rendered by Litematica. |
| `fastMoveLargePlacementVolume` Large placement volume | 32768 (32³) | Placements whose volume (length × width × height) reaches this value defer rewriting the placement world while being moved continuously, and commit the new position after movement stops. When `Take Over All Placements` is disabled, this also determines which placements are taken over. |
| `fastMoveAsyncVerifier` Multithreaded verifier | On | Clicking Schematic Verifier performs a multithreaded scan directly against the placement data without going through the placement world. Results are displayed in Litematica's normal verification UI. |

### Movement

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fastMoveCommitDelay` Commit delay (ms) | 1500 | How long a large placement must remain stationary before its new position is written to the placement world. Until then, features that depend on the placement world, such as Easy Place and block information, still see the old position. Lower values make these features catch up faster, but cause more commits during continuous movement. |
| `fastMoveRenderDelay` Render delay (ms) | 0 | After a placement starts moving, keep it at its original position for this long before rendering it at the new position. Moving again during the wait resets the timer, so intermediate positions during dragging are never rendered, and the corresponding rebuilds are skipped as well. Useful for dragging extremely large placements. |
| `fastMoveSmoothing` Movement smoothing (ms) | 60 | Time constant for movement interpolation. Higher values produce smoother movement but make the placement feel more "laggy"; set to 0 to disable interpolation and jump directly to the new position. |
| `fastMoveSnapDistance` Snap distance (blocks) | 128 | When a single movement exceeds this distance, interpolation is skipped and the placement immediately snaps to the new position, preventing it from sliding all the way across the world. |

### Performance Budgets

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fastMoveUploadKbPerFrame` Upload budget (KB/frame) | 8192 | Maximum amount of mesh data uploaded to the GPU per frame. Excess data is deferred to later frames. Lower values reduce stutter spikes but make the placement appear more slowly. |
| `fastMoveUploadMsPerFrame` Upload budget (ms/frame) | 3.0 | Maximum time spent creating GPU buffers per frame. This takes effect alongside the data-size budget above; uploading stops as soon as either limit is reached. |
| `fastMoveBuildBatchSections` Build batch size (sections) | 32 | Number of 16×16×16 sections built in each mesh-building batch. Batches closer to the camera are built first, with batches distributed across all builder threads for parallel processing. Smaller batches make results appear sooner; partial rebuilds are applied batch by batch. |
| `fastMoveResortsPerFrame` Transparent resorts per frame | 32 | Maximum number of sections containing transparent blocks (glass, water, etc.) that are resorted per frame. Set to 0 to disable sorting; transparent blocks may appear incorrectly ordered from some angles. |
| `fastMoveResortDistance` Transparent resort distance (blocks) | 1.0 | A transparent section is resorted only after the camera has moved more than this distance relative to the section. |
| `fastMoveVerifierMergeMsPerTick` Verifier merge budget (ms/tick) | 50 | Results calculated by verifier threads are merged into Litematica's verifier on the main thread. This is the maximum amount of time spent merging per tick, measured from the start of each tick. Lower values keep the game smoother during verification, but make the results fill in more slowly. |

### Threads

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fastMoveMeshBuilderThreads` Mesh builder threads | 0 (auto) | Number of threads used to build placement meshes. `0` means CPU cores ÷ 4, with a minimum of 1. Takes effect immediately after changing the setting. |
| `fastMoveVerifierThreads` Verifier threads | 0 (auto) | Number of threads used for verification scans. `0` means CPU cores − 1, with a minimum of 1. Takes effect immediately after changing the setting. |

### Debugging

| Option | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fastMoveDebugGizmos` Debug gizmos | Off | Draws gradually fading boxes around mesh sections currently being processed. Amber: rebuild submitted; green: rebuild result applied; gray: both the previous and new positions are air in the real world and were skipped; blue: full placement rebuild. |
| `fastMoveDebugGizmoDuration` Debug gizmo duration (ms) | 800 | How long each debug box remains visible before fading out. |

## Building

- Single version: run `./gradlew build` in the corresponding branch or worktree.
- All versions: run `scripts/build-all.sh`. Generated JARs are collected in `dist/`.

See [PORTING.md](PORTING.md) for details on porting each version.

## Contributors

- Ryan100C (author)
- [wwwzzzxxx](https://github.com/wwwzzzxxx): ports for 1.16.5 – 1.21.11, render delay, and benchmarks
projects.longDescription_zh:
# Litefastica（LitematicaFastMove）

让 Litematica 快到飞起。

特性：
- **独立网格**：每个投影有自己的 GPU 网格（方块、流体、叠加层），移动时只改变绘制位置，而非重建。
- **平滑移动**：显示位置以插值追上实际位置，拖动投影时不再一格一格地跳。
- **推迟提交**：大型投影连续移动时，不会每一步都重写投影世界，停手后才一次性提交。
- **后台构建**：网格在多个线程上按区段分批构建，离相机近的先出现；上传到 GPU 时有每帧预算，不会卡住画面。
- **精确重建**：只有真实世界方块变化处附近的区段会重建；如果一个区段移动前后所在的真实世界都是空气，就直接跳过。
- **多线程校验**：Configure Schematic Placement　里的 Schematic Verifier 改为多线程扫描，结果仍然显示在 Litematica 自己的校验界面里。
- **光影支持**：现在理论上能在任何光影包下正确渲染。

依赖 Litematica、malilib，以及已内嵌的 [EXIT](https://github.com/hotpad100c/emergency-exit)（让投影渲染绕过光影包）。

支持版本：26.3（主分支）、1.21.11、1.21.8、1.21.4、1.21.1、1.20.6、1.20.4、1.20.2、1.20.1、1.19.3、1.18.2、1.17.1、1.16.5（各 `port/<mc>` 分支）。

## 配置项

所有选项都注入到 Litematica 的配置界面（Generic 页，「--- Litematica Fast Move ---」分组下）。

### 基本

| 选项 | 默认 | 作用 |
|---|---|---|
| `fastMoveEnabled` 启用 | 开 | 总开关。关闭后完全回到 Litematica 原本的行为。 |
| `fastMoveTakeoverAllPlacements` 接管所有投影 | 开 | 开启时，所有投影都使用独立网格渲染；关闭时，只接管体积不小于「大型投影体积」的投影，其余仍由 Litematica 渲染。 |
| `fastMoveLargePlacementVolume` 大型投影体积 | 32768（32³） | 体积（长×宽×高）达到这个值的投影，连续移动时推迟重写投影世界，停手后再提交。关闭「接管所有投影」时，它也是决定是否接管的阈值。 |
| `fastMoveAsyncVerifier` 多线程校验 | 开 | 点击 Schematic Verifier 后用多线程扫描，直接读取投影数据，不经过投影世界。结果照常显示在 Litematica 的校验界面里。 |

### 移动手感

| 选项 | 默认 | 作用 |
|---|--|---|
| `fastMoveCommitDelay` 提交延迟（毫秒） | 1500 | 大型投影停止移动多久之后，才把新位置写入投影世界。在这之前，Easy Place、方块信息等依赖投影世界的功能看到的还是旧位置。调小后这些功能更快跟上，但连续移动时提交次数会更多。 |
| `fastMoveRenderDelay` 渲染延迟（毫秒） | 0| 投影移动后，先在原处停留这么久，再画到新位置。等待期间再次移动会重新计时，所以拖动途中的位置一次也不会被画出来，对应的重建也被省掉。适合拖动特别大的投影。 |
| `fastMoveSmoothing` 移动平滑（毫秒） | 60 | 移动插值的时间常数。越大越平滑，但跟随越「拖」；设为 0 关闭插值，直接跳到新位置。 |
| `fastMoveSnapDistance` 瞬移距离（格） | 128 | 一次移动超过这个距离时不做插值，直接瞬移，避免投影从远处一路滑过来。 |

### 性能预算

| 选项 | 默认 | 作用 |
|---|---|---|
| `fastMoveUploadKbPerFrame` 上传预算（KB/帧） | 8192 | 每帧最多上传到 GPU 的网格数据量，超出的留到后续帧。调小能减少卡顿尖峰，但投影出现得更慢。 |
| `fastMoveUploadMsPerFrame` 上传预算（毫秒/帧） | 3.0 | 每帧创建 GPU buffer 最多花费的时间，和上面的数据量预算同时生效，先用完哪个就先停。 |
| `fastMoveBuildBatchSections` 构建批次大小（区段） | 32 | 网格以多少个 16×16×16 区段为一批构建。离相机近的批次先构建，各批分散到所有构建线程并行处理。批次越小，结果出现得越早；局部重建会一批一批地生效。 |
| `fastMoveResortsPerFrame` 每帧半透明重排序数 | 32 | 每帧最多重新排序多少个含半透明方块（玻璃、水等）的区段。设为 0 不排序，半透明方块从某些角度看可能叠错。 |
| `fastMoveResortDistance` 半透明重排序距离（格） | 1.0 | 相机相对某个半透明区段移动超过这个距离后，才重新排序该区段。 |
| `fastMoveVerifierMergeMsPerTick` 校验合并预算（毫秒/tick） | 50 | 校验线程算出的结果在主线程上合并进 Litematica 校验器，这是每个 tick 合并耗时的上限，从 tick 开始时计算。调小后校验期间更流畅，但结果填满得更慢。 |

### 线程

| 选项 | 默认 | 作用 |
|---|---|---|
| `fastMoveMeshBuilderThreads` 网格构建线程数 | 0（自动） | 构建投影网格的线程数，0 表示 CPU 核数 ÷ 4（至少 1）。修改后立即生效。 |
| `fastMoveVerifierThreads` 校验线程数 | 0（自动） | 校验扫描的线程数，0 表示 CPU 核数 − 1（至少 1）。修改后立即生效。 |

### 调试

| 选项 | 默认 | 作用 |
|---|---|---|
| `fastMoveDebugGizmos` 调试框 | 关 | 在正在处理的网格区段上画会逐渐淡出的框。琥珀色：已提交重建；绿色：重建结果已生效；灰色：前后所在的真实世界都是空气，跳过；蓝色：整个投影完整重建。 |
| `fastMoveDebugGizmoDuration` 调试框时长（毫秒） | 800 | 每个调试框从出现到淡出的时长。 |

## 构建

- 单个版本：在对应分支或 worktree 里运行 `./gradlew build`。
- 全部版本：运行 `scripts/build-all.sh`，生成的 jar 收集在 `dist/` 里。

各版本移植的细节见 [PORTING.md](PORTING.md)。

## 贡献者

- Ryan100C（作者）
- [wwwzzzxxx](https://github.com/wwwzzzxxx)：1.16.5 – 1.21.11 各版本移植、渲染延迟、基准测试

projects.longDescription:
# What

Control Player is a **server-side** mod that allows players to swap control with another player or take control of Carpet fake players.

When a swap is active, the two players effectively control each other's bodies.The mod also works well with Carpet mod fake players, allowing real players to temporarily control them.

# Why

This mod makes it possible to observe gameplay from another perspective useful when test mechanics using fake players.

# How

## Main command:

```
/controlPlayer
```

### Swap control

Swap control with another player.

```
/controlPlayer swap <player>
```
Permission level: **2**

---

### Release control

Release your current control state.
```
/controlPlayer release
```
If an admin wants to forcibly release another player:
```
/controlPlayer release <player>
```
Permission level for forced release: **2**

---

### List active swaps

Display all currently active control pairs.

```
/controlPlayer list
```

Permission level: **2**

---

### Check control status

Show whether you are currently controlling another player.

```
/controlPlayer status
```
---
---
## Gamerules

### `showControllerPrefix`

Default: `false`

When enabled, the name of the player currently controlling someone will be displayed ​**after the player's name**​.

This helps identify control relationships more easily, especially when multiple swaps are active.

---

### `permissionSwapsToo`

Default: `false`

When enabled, ​**player permissions will also be swapped together with the bodies**​.

Normally, only the **player control / body** is swapped.
With this rule enabled, the **permission level (such as OP level)** will also be exchanged between the two players.

> **Warning:**
> This can be dangerous on servers, as it may temporarily grant elevated 
> permissions to another player.

# What is this?
This is a visualization mod that renders detailed information about ScheduledTicks in the world, including their type, trigger time, order, and priority.
# How to Use?
First, make sure to install YACL and Mod Menu, and ensure this mod is installed on both the server and the client. 
Then, enter the world, open the settings menu, navigate to Mod Menu, find this mod, and click on its settings. Enable "Main Render" to start visualizing ScheduledTicks.

![Replace this with a description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/1395c87d2191d8e2a5d80eb21a68de00c8c4a954.png)


# Related Commands and Settings
Settings are already explained in the configuration menu and won't be elaborated on here. However, it's worth noting that to prevent the server from sending ScheduledTick data for distant areas (very far away) to the client, the server will check whether any players are within range (default is 20 blocks). This range can be adjusted using the command:

```
/gamerule scheduledTickInformationRange <int>
```
![Replace this with a description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/3ba19f76b7a930f02eb571e1a222e61d281761c8.png)
![Replace this with a description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/41428da2d992c08a2ba1d92b6012bf9cea3b638b.png)

# Additional Explanation and Supported Languages
### Explanation
- Type: Displays the type of the ScheduledTick, indicating whether it's a block tick or a fluid tick.
- SubOrder: Shows the execution order of the ScheduledTick within the current tick, i.e., the sequence among multiple ScheduledTicks.
- Trigger: Indicates how many ticks remain until the ScheduledTick is triggered.
- Priority: Displays the priority level of the ScheduledTick. For more details, refer to this [<documentation>](https://technical-minecraft.fandom.com/wiki/Tile_Tick_Block).
![Replace this with a description](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/a136bdb149992467e5bbfc59799e21c8c112fe73_0.webp) 

### Supported Languages:
The mod currently supports multiple languages, including English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional 
(Taiwan and Hong Kong), and Japanese.

projects.longDescription:
# Simulatica

## What Is This

> Simulatica is **Simulation + Litematica**. It is designed to run block and entity logic within Litematica projections.

## How To Use
- `/simulatica start <litematica file name>` — Start simulating a projection

- `/simulatica stop <litematica file name>` — Stop simulating a projection

- `/simulatica execute <Command to execute in simulated space>` — Execute a command within the simulated space

> Once a simulation has started, switch to **mode 10/10** to interact with the projection.

## How Does It Work

Once at least one simulation has started, a local integrated server is created on the client thread. It initializes a completely empty dimension and loads the target projection to be simulated into it.

Note that this means:

* Projections being simulated cannot overlap.
* Adjacent or near by projections can affect each other during simulation.
* Client-side lag may increase.
* If the simulated integrated server becomes laggy, the client will also be affected.

projects.description: Visualize dust update order in-world.
projects.longDescription:
# VisualDust 

## Commands

All commands are **client‑side only**.  
The server does **not** need to install anything.

| Command | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `/visualdust here <x\|y\|z> [order\|group]` | Add a plane at the player’s current coordinates |
| `/visualdust add <x\|y\|z> <coord> [order\|group]` | Add a plane at a specified coordinate |
| `/visualdust remove <x\|y\|z> <coord>` | Remove a plane |
| `/visualdust clear` | Clear all planes |
| `/visualdust list` | List all current planes |
| `/visualdust mode <order\|group>` | Switch the color mode of all planes |
| `/visualdust alpha <0-100>` | Opacity (%) — default is 70 |
| `/visualdust radius <8-256>` | Baking radius (blocks) — default is 96 |
| `/visualdust query` | Print the update order and group classification of the block under your feet |
| `/visualdust search <d1> [d2..d6]` | Search by update‑order prefix and highlight matching cells on the plane |
| `/visualdust search <d1..> <sizeX> <sizeY> <sizeZ>` | Search inside a cuboid centered on the player; matching blocks appear as cube clouds |
| `/visualdust search` | With no parameters, clear search highlights |

`x` planes cover (Y, Z),  
`y` planes cover (X, Z),  
`z` planes cover (X, Y).  
Vertical range is clamped to world height.

Up to **16 planes** can exist at once.  
Planes on the same axis and same coordinate **replace** each other instead of stacking  
(stacking would cause repeated blending of transparency).

---

## Searching by Update Order

`/visualdust search` takes **1–6 directions**, matching the **prefix** of the block update order:

```
/visualdust search self down south      # Equivalent to O -Y +Z
/visualdust search                      # No parameters = clear highlights
```

Directions may be written as:

- `self` `down` `up` `north` `south` `west` `east`
- or equivalently  
  `O` `-Y` `+Y` `-Z` `+Z` `-X` `+X`

### Structure‑aware autocomplete

Autocomplete only shows directions that can extend the current prefix into a **real existing** update order.  
Impossible structural combinations simply never appear.

Example:

```
(empty)            -> 5 options: O  -Y  +Y  -Z  +Z      ← +X/-X proven never to lead
O                  -> 4 options: -Y  +Y  -Z  +Z
O -Y               -> 1 option: +Z
O -Y +Z            -> 1 option: +X
O -Y +Z +X         -> 1 option: +Y
O -Y +Z +X +Y      -> 2 options: -Z  -X
```

Repeated directions are naturally excluded — once a direction is used, no valid sequence can follow it, so autocomplete shows nothing.

### Why up to 6 directions?

There are 7 elements in the update order.  
The first 6 positions uniquely determine the 7th, so 6 parameters give an exact match.

Manually typing structurally impossible combinations (autocomplete won’t show them, but you can force them) will report **“does not exist”**, e.g.:

```
/visualdust search east   # +X leading — mathematically impossible
```

Matching cells are baked into a separate VertexBuffer and overlaid in bright yellow on top of the plane’s color mode.

---

## Cuboid Search

If you add three sizes after the directions, the mode switches from **plane highlight** to **cube cloud**:

```
/visualdust search O -Y +Z 64 64 64
```

Inside a `sizeX × sizeY × sizeZ` cuboid centered on the player, all matching blocks are rendered as cube clouds.

- Each axis max: **512**
- Max scan volume: **16.77 million blocks (256³)**
- **The center is fixed at the moment you run the command** — it does not follow the player afterward.

---

## Two Color Modes

### **order**
Color based on the full 7‑direction update order using Fourier coloring.  
All **5040 permutations** have unique colors.

### **group**
Color based on the 3‑group classification:

- 6 colors (red/orange/pink variants)  
  - Hue = which group leads  
  - Brightness = order of the remaining two groups
- Blocks not fitting the grouping are colored **gray**  
  (about **2.93%** of all blocks).

# Changelog

## Unreleased

### Sapling growth statistics

Vanilla tree generation is random, so two saplings of the same species rarely produce the same
shape, and there is no easy way to see what a species actually generates. The new
`saplingGrowthStatistics` rule samples every tree that grows from a sapling and turns those samples
into readable statistics.

- New rule **`saplingGrowthStatistics`** (off by default; categories `[YACA]`, `[feature]`,
  `[treefarm]`). While it is enabled, a tree grown from a sapling **places no blocks**: the growth
  is recorded instead, storing the blocks it would have placed together with their offsets from the
  sapling, grouped per species.
- New command **`/treeStats`** (gamemaster permission) - per-species overview: trees sampled, total
  logs, average logs per tree, leaves and beehives.
- **`/treeStats export`** writes an interactive page to `run/tree-growth-stats.html`: a rotatable
  and zoomable 3D view of the sampled blocks, per-block visibility toggles, a layer-by-layer
  profile table and the per-species overview. The page follows the browser language
  (English / 简体中文 / Русский) and falls back to English.
- **`/treeStats grow <pos> <times>`** force-grows the sapling at the given position N times to
  collect samples quickly, with progress shown on a boss bar; **`/treeStats stop`** cancels a
  running sampling.
- **`/treeStats reset`** clears all collected data.
